steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on optic disc and cup segmentation with noisy labels. Explain why annotation noise is a problem here, review multi-expert and label-denoising approaches, then introduce our MPNN method with its pseudo-label module and teacher-student setup, and finish with a contributions list.

  - Self-Calib (cite): divergent + convergent models in loops to find ground truths; better use of multiple annotations -> more impartial model

- Label denoising without extra experts

  - some methods (cite): train multiple networks, pick labels with minimum loss consensus between predictions

  - but: mostly artificially simulated noise and non-expert annotations

  - multiple networks, different initialization, same training set; stop after threshold -> multiple pseudo-labels

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Optic disc and cup segmentation is an important step for automated screening and diagnosis of optic nerve head abnormalities, for example glaucoma. Deep learning has developed rapidly and many models based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have come out, and they show promising performance in medical image segmentation. These methods use their ability to learn intricate patterns and features from a lot of labeled data, and so they can reach high accuracy when segmenting medical images. But the true segmentation boundary of the optic disc and cup is ambiguous, and manual labeling always has some errors, so the annotation often has noise in it. Many studies have shown that label noise can hurt the accuracy of models a lot.

One strategy to reduce the effect of label noise on medical image segmentation is to use annotations from multiple experts. Previous work introduced MRNet, a technique that uses the specialized insight of each rater and treats their expertise as prior knowledge in order to extract high-level semantic features. Self-Calib tries to find ground truths by running divergent and convergent models in loops. It shows a greater ability to use the information from multiple annotations, and the result is a more impartial segmentation model. However, getting segmentation annotations from multiple experts is hard to do. So we need to look at other methods.

- Label denoising without extra experts
  - two steps: identify noisy labels, then discard them or refine with pseudo-labels
  - some methods train multiple networks, pick labels with minimum loss consensus between predictions
  - others use Confident Learning modules to find noisy labels, plus a refinement module
  - but mostly simulated noise / non-expert annotations; nothing on noise from ambiguous OD/OC boundaries
- Our method: MPNN
  - MPGGD module: multiple networks, different initialization, stop after threshold -> multiple pseudo-labels
  - consistent pixels = clean, rest = noisy
  - teacher-student: segmentation loss on clean pixels, consistency loss on noisy pixels with teacher (multiple uncertainties); teacher updated by EMA
- Contributions
  - first OD/OC method from label-denoising perspective
  - MPGGD separates reliable/unreliable information, avoids negative impact of label noise

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Optic disc and cup segmentation is an important step for automated screening and diagnosis of optic nerve head abnormalities, for example glaucoma. Deep learning has developed rapidly and many models based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have come out, and they show promising performance in medical image segmentation. These methods use their ability to learn intricate patterns and features from a lot of labeled data, and so they can reach high accuracy when segmenting medical images. But the true segmentation boundary of the optic disc and cup is ambiguous, and manual labeling always has some errors, so the annotation often has noise in it. Many studies have shown that label noise can hurt the accuracy of models a lot.

One strategy to reduce the effect of label noise on medical image segmentation is to use annotations from multiple experts. Previous work introduced MRNet, a technique that uses the specialized insight of each rater and treats their expertise as prior knowledge in order to extract high-level semantic features. Self-Calib tries to find ground truths by running divergent and convergent models in loops. It shows a greater ability to use the information from multiple annotations, and the result is a more impartial segmentation model. However, getting segmentation annotations from multiple experts is hard to do. So we need to look at other methods.

A series of label-denoising strategies have been proposed to deal with noisy labels in segmentation tasks without adding more expert labels. They usually have two steps: first the noisy labels are identified in some way, and then they are either discarded or refined using pseudo-labels. Some methods train multiple networks and choose labels with the minimum loss consensus between the network predictions for training. Other methods use Confident Learning modules to find the noisy labels and then a refinement module to process them. But these works mostly use artificially simulated noisy labels and annotations made by non-experts. There is no specific research yet on the annotation noise that comes from ambiguous boundaries in optic disc and cup segmentation.

In this paper we propose a new label-denoising method, the Multiple Pseudo-labels Noise-aware Network (MPNN), for accurate optic disc and cup segmentation. For the label noise issue we propose the Multiple Pseudo-labels Generation and Guided Denoising (MPGGD) module. We train multiple networks with different initialization on the same training set, and stop training after a certain threshold, which gives us multiple pseudo-labels for the training set. Then the pixels whose labels are consistent on all the pseudo-labels are taken as clean pixels, and the other pixels are taken as noisy pixels. MPNN also has a teacher-student architecture. The student network learns by (i) minimizing the segmentation loss on the clean pixels and (ii) minimizing the consistency loss on the noisy pixels with the teacher model with multiple uncertainties. The teacher network is updated from the student network parameters with the Exponential Moving Average (EMA). Our contributions are:

- To our knowledge, MPNN is the first method that improves the segmentation accuracy of the optic disc and cup from the point of view of label denoising.

- We propose the MPGGD module. It separates reliable and unreliable information, gives the network accurate prior information, and avoids the negative effect of label noise on the network.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Optic disc and cup segmentation is an important step in the automated screening and diagnosis of optic nerve head abnormalities such as glaucoma. With the rapid development of deep learning, various models based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have emerged and shown promising performance in medical image segmentation. These methods [1,2,3] leverage their capacity to learn intricate patterns and features from extensive labeled data, which enables them to achieve high accuracy in segmenting medical images. However, due to the inherent ambiguity of the true segmentation boundary in optic disc and cup segmentation and the inevitable errors in manual labeling, the annotation often contains noise. Numerous studies [4,5] have indicated that label noise can significantly affect the accuracy of models.

To mitigate the impact of label noise on medical image segmentation, one strategy is to use multiple expert annotations. Ji et al. [6] introduced MRNet, a technique that capitalizes on the specialized insight of individual raters, treating their expertise as prior knowledge to extract high-level semantic features. Self-Calib [7] attempts to find ground truths by running divergent and convergent models in loops, showing a greater capacity for exploiting information from multiple annotations, which leads to a more impartial segmentation model. However, obtaining segmentation annotations from multiple experts is a challenging task, so it is necessary to explore other available methods.

Without introducing additional expert labels, a series of label-denoising strategies have been proposed to cope with noisy labels in segmentation tasks. These strategies typically involve two steps: first, noisy labels are identified using various methods, and then they are either discarded or refined using pseudo-labels. Some methods [8,9,10,11] train multiple networks and select labels with the minimum loss consensus between network predictions for training. Other methods [4,12,13] use Confident Learning [14] modules to find noisy labels and a refinement module to process them. However, these studies often involve artificially simulated noisy labels and annotations from non-experts, and there has not been specific research on annotation noise caused by ambiguous boundaries in optic disc and cup segmentation.

In this paper, we propose a novel label-denoising method, the Multiple Pseudo-labels Noise-aware Network (MPNN), for accurate optic disc and cup segmentation. To address label noise, we propose the Multiple Pseudo-labels Generation and Guided Denoising (MPGGD) module. We use multiple networks with different initialization to fit the same training set and stop training after reaching a certain threshold, obtaining multiple pseudo-labels for the training set. The pixels whose labels are consistent across all the pseudo-labels are then considered clean pixels, and the rest are considered noisy pixels. Furthermore, MPNN uses a teacher-student architecture, in which the student network learns by (i) minimizing the segmentation loss on the clean pixels and (ii) minimizing the consistency loss on the noisy pixels with the teacher model with multiple uncertainties. The teacher network is updated from the parameters of the student network using the Exponential Moving Average (EMA). Our contributions are as follows:

- To the best of our knowledge, MPNN is the first method to improve the segmentation accuracy of the optic disc and cup from the perspective of label denoising.

- We propose the MPGGD module, which separates reliable and unreliable information, provides accurate prior information for the network and avoids the negative impact of label noise on the network.
